author: Carlos Martinez
title: GTA 6 Driving: A Sim Racer's First Hours on Xbox Series X
description: A sim racer's first hours of GTA 6 driving on Xbox Series X with a controller: the vehicles, five driving moments, and how the stream was set up without a capture card.

sections.p: I race in iRacing, so I looked at GTA 6 driving the way a sim racer does. I played the first hours live on launch day, on an Xbox Series X with a controller, blind, with no guide open. This is a log of what happened behind the wheel, not a review and not a handling test.
This is fan content. It is not affiliated with Rockstar Games.

sections.html: GTA 6 LIVE: Sim Racer Plays for the First Time

sections.p: The full stream is above. It runs 2 hours and 5 minutes, live on the @realtape YouTube channel on November 19, 2026.

In these hours I drove several kinds of vehicle. There were pickup trucks, a red retro sports car, a dark retro sports coupe, a motorcycle and a grey SUV. At one point I took a car off a tow truck. The world around them looks like a sunny coastal region, with palm trees, highways, long bridges over water and run-down streets.
I did not set out to test cars. Much of the driving happened with a police wanted level on, so these are chase moments, not calm laps. Keep that in mind when you watch.

sections.h2: Five driving moments from the stream

sections.p: I cut five Shorts and Reels from the stream. Each one is a single driving moment, with no story context needed.

list: I Hit a Gate at Full Speed in GTA 6. A red retro sports car runs along a road and over a bridge with the police on its tail. It reaches an industrial site with a closed gate and hits it. Watch the Short · Watch the Reel

GTA 6 Bike Crash Sends the Rider Flying. A rider on a motorcycle goes down a sunny road past traffic. At an intersection a pickup appears beside the bike, the game switches to a slow crash camera, and the rider is thrown into a flip. The rider lands and stands up. Watch the Short · Watch the Reel

Sim Racer Slides a Retro Coupe in GTA 6. A dark retro coupe cuts across grass and a corner, brushes some plants and a pole, then slides sideways in front of a gas station and drives on. Watch the Short · Watch the Reel
Sideways in a Pickup Truck in GTA 6. A beige pickup comes into a junction and swings hard around it, then drives on under an overpass between other cars. Watch the Short · Watch the Reel
GTA 6 Gunfight in a Car Lot Ends Badly. The most graphic of the five, so it comes last. It is a third-person gunfight among rows of parked cars in a fenced lot. Watch the Short · Watch the Reel

sections.p: The Shorts are on YouTube @realtape and the Reels are on Instagram @realiracing.

sections.h2: A sim racer on a controller

sections.p: I am used to a wheel, pedals and force feedback. Here I had a controller and a game that does not try to be a simulator. I will not give handling numbers or a verdict, because I did not measure anything. What I can say is what the footage shows: cars that slide sideways, cut across grass and hit gates and poles. A proper handling breakdown needs more hours than this.
If you race in iRacing, you will see how different this is. In iRacing a big slide usually means I have made a mistake. In the gas station clip I slid sideways and kept driving.

sections.h2: How I streamed GTA 6 from Chile

sections.p: Here is the setup. I do not use a capture card. The Xbox picture reaches OBS through Xbox Remote Play in a browser window on the PC. OBS captures that window and streams 1080p60 to YouTube. I use a Logitech C920 webcam for the facecam and a USB audio interface for the microphone.
It worked, but it has real downsides that I saw during the stream:

list: Remote Play pauses when its window loses focus, so clicking another window can freeze the picture.
It disconnects after a long idle. A disconnect near the end of my session ended the feed.
There is picture delay if you play from the PC screen.

sections.p: The better way to run this is to play on the TV that is wired to the Xbox, and use the PC only as a mirror for OBS. The cleaner fix is a capture card, which takes the Remote Play window out of the chain. If you plan to stream a console, that is the route to look at.
There are story moments in the stream that I kept out of this post and out of the clip titles, so I do not spoil anything for you. The clips only show driving and crashing.
Watch the full stream above, then check the Shorts and Reels. More sim racing posts are on the blog, and my racing rig is on the My Rig page.

faqs.q: Is this a GTA 6 handling review?
faqs.a: No. It is a log of my first hours driving on launch day, played blind with a controller. I did not measure anything, so there are no handling numbers or scores.

faqs.q: What did you play GTA 6 on?
faqs.a: An Xbox Series X with a controller. The stream is on the @realtape YouTube channel and runs 2 hours and 5 minutes.

faqs.q: How do you stream an Xbox to YouTube without a capture card?
faqs.a: The Xbox picture reaches OBS through Xbox Remote Play in a browser window on the PC. OBS captures that window and streams 1080p60. Remote Play pauses when its window loses focus and can disconnect after a long idle, so a capture card is the cleaner fix.
